title: edit ignores the KIND it was given and answers about a thread, so 'edit issue 0056 --path' returns thread ST0056's file at rc=0
body:
**`intent edit issue 0056 --path` PRINTS THREAD ST0056'S `info.md`, AT rc=0.** Issue 0056 exists and is a real, closed, high-severity issue. The operator named an ISSUE, the tool answered about a THREAD, reported success, and handed back a path they may then edit.

**THIS IS `0149`'S CLASS ONE STEP WORSE.** `0149` parsed the kind, discarded it, and REFUSED about a steel thread the caller never named. This does the same discard and SUCCEEDS. A refusal is survivable; a wrong path at rc=0 is what someone opens.

=== THREE DEFECTS, MEASURED TOGETHER ===

**ONE -- `<KIND>` IS NEVER READ.** `render.rs:1399` is `match arg(m, "address") { Ok(a) => a, Err(_) => thread_arg(m, "id")? }`. **`address` is `explore`'s argument name; `edit`'s argument is named `id`** (`surface/dispatch-table.json`: `edit` and `browse` declare `id`, `explore` declares `address`). So the probe always errs, always falls through to `thread_arg` -- the THREAD parser -- and the kind the operator typed reaches nothing. Found by cc; mechanism identified by vc.

**TWO -- THE DECLARED `address-or-id` TYPE IS NOT HONOURED.** The row's own note reads *`address::promote` stays the one door*. `thread_arg` is not that door: it splits on `/` and reads `intent:` as a thread id, so `intent edit st intent://threads/ST0056 --path` refuses with *`intent:` is not a steel thread id*. **The declaration and the implementation disagree, and the row is the one that is right.**

**THREE -- THE `kind` ENUM IS NOT VALIDATED.** `intent edit banana ST0056 --path` prints ST0056's path at rc=0. The table declares `values: [st, wp, issue]` and nothing enforces them -- the same declaration-versus-implementation gap `--format` carried until `07ad9876`.

=== WHY IT SURVIVED ===

**Every spelling an operator naturally reaches for is a THREAD spelling, so the fallback is right by accident on the common path.** `edit st ST0056` works, `edit st 56` works, and `THREAD_DIGITS == ISSUE_DIGITS == 4` means `edit issue 0056` produces a well-formed thread id rather than an error. **The wrong answer is only visible when the operator names an issue whose number is also a thread number -- and 48 of 69 thread numbers are also issue numbers** (vc's measurement), so the failure is common and silent rather than rare and loud.

=== BLAST RADIUS ===

`--path` prints a path. `--editor` OPENS it. So the same defect under `--editor` puts an operator in the wrong file with no indication they are not where they asked to be.

`browse` is declared with the identical `kind` + `id: address-or-id` shape and is UNWIRED (rc=2), so it carries no defect today -- but whoever wires it must use the same door or the two spellings of one verb diverge on which forms they accept.

=== RELEASE RELEVANCE ===

`ST0064` `AC-01.5` makes the menubar app a CLIENT of the one resolver, handing `intent edit` an `intent://` URL and opening what comes back. Defect TWO is why it cannot: ic measured both candidate doors failing in opposite directions -- `explore` accepts the URL and needs a TERMINAL a `.app` does not have, `edit` is pipe-safe and cannot take the URL.

=== PROVENANCE, MEASURED AGAINST THE SHIPPED BINARY -- AND IT CORRECTS THE ACCOUNT ABOVE ===

**The mechanism stated above -- _`address` is `explore`'s argument name_ -- is true today and is NOT the cause.** It was `edit`'s OWN argument name. Driven against the shipped v3.0.0 keg, which dc established is on this machine and read-only at the tag commit `80d8b2ca`:

    /opt/homebrew/Cellar/intent/3.0.0_1/bin/intent edit --help
    -> Usage: intent edit <ADDRESS> [FILE]

and the tag's own table agrees -- `edit` declared `[('address', 'address-or-id'), ('file', 'enum')]`, **one positional, named `address`.**

**SO THE PROBE WAS CORRECT WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN AND WAS LEFT BEHIND BY A RENAME.** `<KIND>` and the rename of `address` to `id` arrived after the tag, at `0f41dce1` (*Safety checkin prior to HV being afk*). The `Err(_) => thread_arg(m, "id")` fallback predates it, at `58979836`, and was added for a different and legitimate reason: `intent st edit <id>` is thread-scoped and shares this function.

**THE FALLBACK IS WHAT MADE THE RENAME SILENT.** Without it the probe would have failed loudly the moment the argument was renamed. With it, `arg(m, "address")` simply started erring every time and the thread parser absorbed every call -- so a rename that should have been a compile-or-runtime break became a wrong answer at rc=0. **A defensive fallback added for one caller swallowed a defect belonging to another.**

**AND IT DID NOT SHIP.** v3.0.0 has no `<KIND>` to ignore, so this defect is post-tag and belongs to 3.0.1's window, not to the release. Recorded because the first version of this issue reasoned from the code in front of me and would have read as a shipped defect to anyone auditing later.

**METHOD NOTE, OWED TO dc:** every claim above was a date-or-code inference until the keg was driven, and the measurement was available the whole time. dc published six false shipped-defect claims sourced the same way and found them by driving that binary.
